gaps.sentence: There were ___ than twenty people at the meeting.
We haven't got ___ chairs for everyone.
gaps.explanation: 'Enough chairs' means a sufficient number; 'too' before the noun would give the wrong meaning and position.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the workforce is part-time now.
gaps.hint: pattern: ___ of + specific group; singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Half of the workforce is ...' is the correct pattern; 'the half of' is not used in this position.

gaps.sentence: A ___ of people complained about the noise.
gaps.hint: the article 'A' is already in the sentence
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of people' is the fixed phrase; 'a lots of' and 'a plenty of' are wrong, and 'a great' needs 'deal ... of'.
'Several charges' means more than two; the other options are used only with uncountable nouns.

gaps.sentence: She made very ___ mistakes in the essay, so she nearly got full marks.
gaps.explanation: 'Very few mistakes' means almost none, which explains the high mark; 'mistakes' is countable.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the students has been given a personal timetable.
gaps.hint: this is the only option that can be followed by 'of' and take a singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each of the students has ...' is correct; 'every' cannot take 'of' here and 'all/both' need a plural verb.

gaps.sentence: ___ everyone in the office passed the safety test.
gaps.hint: the only adverb that can modify 'everyone'
gaps.explanation: 'Almost everyone' is the standard pattern; 'each', 'all' and 'every' cannot directly precede 'everyone'.
